t: For the purchase, manufacture, repair, and installation of necessary miscellaneous equipment and supplies for the field service not otherwise provided for; not to exceed $1,500 for the purchase of atlases and geographical and technical works; not to exceed $239,000 for personal services, including seventeen traveling mechanicians; rental of canceling machines and motors, mechanical mail-handling apparatus, and other labor-saving devices; and travel expenses; $11,300,000, of which $750,000 shall be available exclusively for the development, manufacture, and purchase of modern mechanical postal devices to improve and facilitate mail handling, financial operations, and other postal functions: Provided, That the Postmaster General may authorize the sale to the public of post-route maps and rural-delivery maps at the cost of printing and 10 per centum thereof added.

fable.w: This is an appropriation for postal equipment, supplies, personal services, and mechanical devices. The tempting reading is that the reference to "the public" signals participation, but it only authorizes selling maps to the public, which is a commercial transaction and not consultation on a federal decision. No outside party is consulted, heard, placed on an advisory body, or given a right to sue.
fable.s: Provided, That the Postmaster General may authorize the sale to the public of post-route maps and rural-delivery maps at the cost of printing and 10 per centum thereof added.

qwen_block.w: This section is an appropriations provision detailing funding for equipment, supplies, personal services, and travel expenses for the Post Office. It does not require consultation, coordination, or participation from outside parties in any federal decision-making process. The mention of selling maps to the public is a commercial transaction, not a participatory mechanism in government decision-making.
qwen_block.s: For the purchase, manufacture, repair, and installation of necessary miscellaneous equipment and supplies for the field service not otherwise provided for; not to exceed $1,500 for the purchase of atlases and geographical and technical works; not to exceed $239,000 for personal services, including seventeen traveling mechanicians; rental of canceling machines and motors, mechanical mail-handling apparatus, and other labor-saving devices; and travel expenses; $11,300,000, of which $750,000 shall be available exclusively for the development, manufacture, and purchase of modern mechanical postal devices to improve and facilitate mail handling, financial operations, and other postal functions: Provided, That the Postmaster General may authorize the sale to the public of post-route maps and rural-delivery maps at the cost of printing and 10 per centum thereof added.

opus.w: This is an appropriations provision for postal equipment, staff and supplies. The only mention of the public is a power to sell maps to them at cost. That is a sale, not a way for outsiders to be consulted on or take part in a federal decision. The section has no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue, so it does not involve participation.
opus.s: Provided, That the Postmaster General may authorize the sale to the public of post-route maps and rural-delivery maps at the cost of printing and 10 per centum thereof added.
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading:** The section mentions selling maps "to the public," which can look like the public being involved with the federal government. That fails the definition. Selling maps at cost is a transaction, not consultation with outsiders before a federal decision. Nothing else here involves outside parties: no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking authority or right to sue. The rest of the section is spending authority for equipment, staff and travel.

qwen_chat.w: This section primarily details appropriations for equipment, supplies, and personnel within the federal government. The only mention of the public is regarding the sale of maps, which is a commercial transaction rather than a participatory process involving consultation or coordination before a federal decision. Selling goods to the public does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: Provided, That the Postmaster General may authorize the sale to the public of post-route maps and rural-delivery maps at the cost of printing and 10 per centum thereof added.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that selling maps to the public constitutes a form of public interaction or participation. However, this is a commercial transaction (sale of goods), not a process where the public consults with or influences a federal decision. The definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits or grants, and by extension, simple commercial sales do not constitute "participation" in the sense of consulting or coordinating with outsiders before a decision is made. The rest of the section is purely about internal appropriations and personnel.
